alex: Heads-up — seeing a spike of 503s from allocator pool A at ~11:30. KV hit-rate fell ~18% and kernel selector tripped to the slow fallback kernels. Leaving notes here so we can land a short, repeatable playbook.

maya: Saw that too. Topline: P95 latency doubled, batch sizes shrank automatically, and workload churn increased KV churn. CC @sam for perf numbers.

sam: Initial idea: "eviction staircase" + request dialback. Short version: 1) soft eviction at 70% headroom (evict old prefixes, preserve hot keys), 2) medium eviction at 85% (more aggressive prefix trim + drop cached attention segments), 3) hard eviction at 92% (reject/bail requests with clear 429 + force model fallback). Also reduce per-request workspace factor as we cross thresholds.

julia: Sounds good. Can we codify thresholds as config flags so oncall can flip quickly? Suggest keys: `allocator.eviction.stairs=[70,85,92]` and `runtime.request_shaper.max_tokens_factor` (0.8 -> 0.5 depending on stage).

alex: Example CLI to flip circuit quickly: 
```
redwoodctl feature toggle allocator-stairs --env prod --value on
redwoodctl config apply --patch '{"runtime.request_shaper.max_tokens_factor":0.6}'
```
(ops-runbook steps, 2-line).

sam: For kernel fallback, prefer switching to the quantized variant on the same GPU before falling back to slower kernels — keeps latency predictable. Policy: if eviction stage == hard then route to q4f model variant that uses <60% workspace.

maya: Also add a short-lived route-level throttle for non-SLA routes: `route.throttle.window=5s,route.throttle.p95=0.6` — buys time for the allocator to reclaim.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Feature `allocator-stairs` toggled ON by maya at 2024-04-05T11:36:20Z :white_check_mark:

alex: After flip: error rate dropped ~65% in 8 minutes, KV hit-rate stabilized. P95 still elevated but avoiding 503 cascade. Good candidate for standard playbook.

julia: Follow-ups to add to runbook: - automated telemetry alert when headroom crosses 70/85/92 - a synthetic traffic job that verifies Q-model latency before routing - post-incident note to evaluate workspace sizing per model family.

sam: I'll draft a mini-runbook and include the quick CLI blocks + rollback steps. Will post PR to `eng-runtime/runbooks` in ~30m.

maya: Thanks all. If oncall sees the 85->92 climb, enable medium eviction first, then trigger q-model routing. Keep @alex looped. :thumbsup:

alex: Adding final log snippet for context: `alloc:poolA headroom=18% evict=prefixes oldest=1200ms kernel_swap=slow->q4f` — helps triage later.
